prompt.brief: Design a cost-efficient e-commerce backend that handles catalog browsing, inventory, checkout, payments, fulfillment, and traffic spikes while preserving order correctness.
successSignals: Define catalog, inventory reservation, cart, order, payment, shipment, and return boundaries with idempotent state transitions.
Keep browse reads highly cacheable while making checkout strongly correct around stock, totals, payment authorization, and order creation.
Design for flash-sale bursts, hot products, asynchronous fulfillment, payment webhooks, retries, reconciliation, and dead-letter recovery.
Explain security, fraud controls, observability, cost guardrails, and degraded browsing or checkout behavior.

functional: Browse and search products, manage carts, reserve inventory, create orders, authorize/capture/refund payments, and track fulfillment.
Support authenticated customers, guest checkout, promotions, tax/shipping quotes, seller/admin updates, and order history.
Make retries safe, reconcile payment and inventory mismatches, audit sensitive actions, and recover from partial workflow failures.
nonFunctional: Meet p95 browse latency under 200ms and checkout confirmation under 2 seconds excluding external payment latency.
Scale from quiet periods to 100x flash-sale bursts without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 100x traffic bursts; 50k checkout attempts per minute
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Cost-efficient e-commerce backend commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Cost-efficient e-commerce backend writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Cost-efficient e-commerce backend version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Cost-efficient e-commerce backend by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Cost-efficient e-commerce backend work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Cost-efficient e-commerce backend projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Cost-efficient e-commerce backend projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Cost-efficient e-commerce backend records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Cost-efficient e-commerce backend latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
